description:
src/memory.rs:247-259 — same struct, two builder/init methods with
inconsistent argument types:

    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_account(self, account_id: &str) -> Self {
        self.register_account(&Id::from(account_id));
        self
    }

    pub fn register_account(&self, account_id: &Id) {
        ...
    }

with_account accepts &str (uses Id::from internally), register_account
accepts &Id. A consumer who reads the documentation expecting one
convention writes:

    let id = Id::from("acc1");
    let backend = MemoryBackend::new().with_account(&id);   // type error

…or the inverse:

    let backend = MemoryBackend::new();
    backend.register_account("acc1");   // type error

Both errors compile-fail; not a runtime hazard. But the friction is
real for cookie-cutter test setup that switches between calendars
and mail-server (mail-server's register_account is also &Id).

Note the inline test_support::MockBackend at src/lib.rs:272 has a
THIRD convention: new_with_account(account_id: &str) — neither &str-
adapter-internally NOR &Id directly. So a contributor writing test
fixtures across MockBackend (test_support) and MemoryBackend faces:

  - MockBackend::new_with_account(&str)
  - MemoryBackend::with_account(&str)        // &str adapter
  - MemoryBackend::register_account(&Id)     // &Id direct
  - MemoryBackend::seed_object(account_id: &str, ...)   // &str
  - JmapBackend::account_exists(... account_id: &Id ...)   // &Id (trait)

…five "give me an account id" surfaces in the same crate.

What goes wrong for the caller: every fixture write triggers a brief
context-switch ("which one wants &Id, which wants &str?"). A
cookie-cutter test author writing one helper that accepts an &str and
calls into multiple MemoryBackend methods has to call Id::from twice
where the consistency could be one allocation.

Fix: pick one convention and apply consistently. Two coherent options:

  (a) All public MemoryBackend constructors and seed methods take
      `impl Into<Id>` or `&str`. The current with_account pattern wins,
      register_account adapts internally.

  (b) All take `&Id`. The current register_account pattern wins,
      with_account is dropped or restricted.

(a) is more ergonomic for test setup; (b) matches the workspace-wide
canonical convention (jmap_types::Id is the wire type).

This finding is taste-adjacent — file as opinion if maintainer prefers
to keep both conventions and document the difference. P3 because no
correctness is at stake and the compile errors are clear.
title: MemoryBackend::with_account takes &str but register_account takes &Id; argument-type inconsistency within the same struct
